verdict.rationale: Fastmail's developer page documents a public JMAP API. It publishes a session endpoint at api.fastmail.com that advertises capabilities, accounts and API URLs, supports API-token or OAuth/Bearer auth, and points to the IETF RFCs as the full specification. JMAP lets a client query, fetch and send in a single methodCalls request, with push via EventSource or WebPush, so a program can drive the mailbox. Probes found no OpenAPI or llms.txt file, but the story only asks for a documented public API, so that does not count against it. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of driving Fastmail through the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The JMAP session resource can be found at https://api.fastmail.com/jmap/session
POST a `methodCalls` array. Query, fetch, and send, all in one HTTP request.
Standard OAuth 2.0 or Bearer tokens. No custom auth protocol to implement.
No patents. No fees. Fully documented.
